════ 1. SPEC.MD PER-LINE DELTAS ════

R1a · spec.md:64 (R24) — parity claim narrowed to pin identity + config.property_path; discovery evidence/retry guidance declared refresh-path; publication_impact dropped (only AD16 :193 / AD18 :197 carry it, both operation refresh; AD21 :203 licenses only config_revision/trigger on an r7 record).
CURRENT:
- R24 (owner rulings 10, 18): The log shows a configuration edit reaching the running process: refresh records name the configuration revision and trigger they used. SIGHUP reload and periodic refresh report IDENTICAL pin diagnostic detail — identity, source location, discovery evidence, publication impact, retry guidance; no path is the only way to obtain the useful error.
REPLACEMENT:
- R24 (owner rulings 10, 18): The log shows a configuration edit reaching the running process: refresh records name the configuration revision and trigger they used. A pin rejection on SIGHUP reload and on periodic refresh reports the same core pin diagnostic detail — pin identity (server, tool) and source location (`config.property_path`); discovery evidence and retry guidance are refresh-path records (AD16–AD18) and are not asserted on the reload path; no path is the only way to obtain the useful error.

R1b · spec.md:260 (AC11-1) — names the reload-side carrier and the compared key forms, so it is writable as a deterministic test.
CURRENT:
- AC11-1 (11/AC-1; R24): a pin rejection on SIGHUP reload and on periodic refresh reports the same core detail — pin identity (server, tool), source location (`config.property_path`), publication impact (`publication_impact`); discovery evidence (chunked `discovered_tools`) and retry guidance (`next_attempt_ms`) remain refresh-path records (AD18/AD16/AD17) and are not asserted on the reload path. test.
REPLACEMENT:
- AC11-1 (11/AC-1; R24): a pin rejection on SIGHUP reload and on periodic refresh reports the same core detail — pin identity (server, tool) and source location (`config.property_path`); `publication_impact` is no longer part of the compared set (the rejection event itself states the impact; refresh-side `publication_impact` stays asserted by AC09-7). Compared carriers and key forms — reload: `config_reload_rejected` (AD7) carrying the Diagnostics-renderer pin attribution (AD3/AD4) as `config.pin_server`, `config.pin_tool`, `config.property_path`; refresh: `pin_blocker_detail` (AD18) carrying typed `server`, `config.pin_tool`, `config.property_path`. Discovery evidence (chunked `discovered_tools`) and retry guidance (`next_attempt_ms`) remain refresh-path records (AD18/AD16/AD17) and are not asserted on the reload path. test.

R2 · spec.md:251 (AC09-5) — drop the false "the design's existing ≤64 bound" attribution (the design's only ≤64 is the pin ceiling); the bound becomes this AC's own oracle requirement.
CURRENT:
- AC09-5 (09/AC-5; R21): for each server with a missing pin, `discovered_tools` listed; large lists split across records sharing `refresh_id`, `server`, `chunk_index`/`chunk_count`; each chunk record carries at most 64 `discovered_tools` names (the design's existing ≤64 bound), so `chunk_count` ≥ 2 whenever a server's listing exceeds 64; no silent truncation. test.
REPLACEMENT:
- AC09-5 (09/AC-5; R21): for each server with a missing pin, `discovered_tools` listed; large lists split across records sharing `refresh_id`, `server`, `chunk_index`/`chunk_count`; each chunk record carries at most 64 `discovered_tools` names (this acceptance criterion's own oracle bound, asserted per chunk record), so `chunk_count` ≥ 2 whenever a server's listing exceeds 64; no silent truncation. test.

R3 · spec.md:195 (AD17) — agree with the AD20 correction: failure_stage is not a new key. Only the parenthetical after the closed set changes; the rest of the line is reproduced verbatim.
CURRENT:
[AUTO-DECISION] AD17 — discovery attribution event (T10): `upstream_discovery_failed`, operation `refresh`, level `warn`, outcome `failure`; typed `server` field; `failure_stage` ∈ closed set {`dns`, `connect`, `tls`, `auth`, `initialize`, `tools_list`} (new shared-vocabulary key; the HTTP lane's `failure_stage` slot already precedents the name); `failure_reason` = bounded cause category incl. timeout classes; `http_status` (REUSED whitelist key) where applicable; `endpoint` = sanitized `scheme://host:port/path` only (R8 by construction); nested `error` with code = the `RefreshReason*` class (`upstream_unavailable`/`discovery_failed`/`client_missing`), retryability: `client_missing` → kind `configuration`, retryable false, remediation "correct the server configuration or credentials"; others → kind `dependency`, retryable true; `next_attempt_ms` present iff an automatic retry is scheduled (R23).
REPLACEMENT:
[AUTO-DECISION] AD17 — discovery attribution event (T10): `upstream_discovery_failed`, operation `refresh`, level `warn`, outcome `failure`; typed `server` field; `failure_stage` ∈ closed set {`dns`, `connect`, `tls`, `auth`, `initialize`, `tools_list`} (NOT a new shared-vocabulary key: the name already exists in the r7 109-name union as HTTP-lane slot 27 (AD2) and is reused with unchanged semantics per AD20); `failure_reason` = bounded cause category incl. timeout classes; `http_status` (REUSED whitelist key) where applicable; `endpoint` = sanitized `scheme://host:port/path` only (R8 by construction); nested `error` with code = the `RefreshReason*` class (`upstream_unavailable`/`discovery_failed`/`client_missing`), retryability: `client_missing` → kind `configuration`, retryable false, remediation "correct the server configuration or credentials"; others → kind `dependency`, retryable true; `next_attempt_ms` present iff an automatic retry is scheduled (R23).

R4 · spec.md:240 (AC08-1) — exactly one catalog_refresh_failed record, so the oracle cannot collide with AD18's per-pin records.
CURRENT:
- AC08-1 (08/AC-1; R20, R22, R25): a refresh pass whose candidate is rejected emits one failure record (`catalog_refresh_failed`) at the AD16-pinned level — warn when `catalog_state` is `retained_published`, error when `none_available` — with debug disabled. test.
REPLACEMENT:
- AC08-1 (08/AC-1; R20, R22, R25): a refresh pass whose candidate is rejected emits exactly one pass-level failure record, `catalog_refresh_failed` (per-pin `pin_blocker_detail` records are additional and not counted by this oracle), at the AD16-pinned level — warn when `catalog_state` is `retained_published`, error when `none_available` — with debug disabled. test.

════ 2. TICKET WHOLE-LINE REPLACEMENTS ════

issues/11-path-parity-and-logger-fallback.md:7 (What-to-build prose; mirrors R1)
CURRENT:
SIGHUP reload and periodic refresh report the same core pin diagnostic detail: identities, configuration source locations and publication impact; chunked discovery evidence and retry guidance are refresh-path records. No path may be the only way to obtain the useful error, so an operator never needs to send a signal to a running process to learn what a pinned tool rejection means.
REPLACEMENT:
SIGHUP reload and periodic refresh report the same core pin diagnostic detail: identities and configuration source locations (`pins[i]` property path); chunked discovery evidence and retry guidance are refresh-path records. No path may be the only way to obtain the useful error, so an operator never needs to send a signal to a running process to learn what a pinned tool rejection means.

issues/11-path-parity-and-logger-fallback.md:12 (AC-1; mirrors AC11-1)
CURRENT:
- [ ] AC-1: A pin rejection on a SIGHUP reload and on a periodic refresh reports the same core detail — pin identity, source location (`pins[i]` property path), publication impact; discovery evidence and retry guidance remain refresh-path records.
REPLACEMENT:
- [ ] AC-1: A pin rejection on a SIGHUP reload and on a periodic refresh reports the same core detail — pin identity and source location (`pins[i]` property path); discovery evidence and retry guidance remain refresh-path records.

issues/09-pin-blocker-detail.md:7 (What-to-build prose; mirrors AC09-2)
CURRENT:
A failed pin check names every blocking pin, not just the first. Reporting one pin per attempt forces a fix-edit-restart cycle per pin, which is the loop this ticket removes. Each unresolved mandatory pin is reported with its safe server and tool identity and its configuration source location - file, property path, one-based line and column - so the operator edits the file directly instead of searching it.
REPLACEMENT:
A failed pin check names every blocking pin, not just the first. Reporting one pin per attempt forces a fix-edit-restart cycle per pin, which is the loop this ticket removes. Each unresolved mandatory pin is reported with its safe server and tool identity and its configuration source location - the pin's `pins[i]` property path - so the operator edits the file directly instead of searching it.

issues/10-discovery-attribution-and-readiness-reason.md:17 (What-to-build prose; mirrors AC10-4 / AD17 iff-condition)
CURRENT:
The record also states the recovery expectation: whether an automatic retry is scheduled or the configuration or credentials must be corrected, together with the next attempt time. Repeating on the refresh interval is not evidence that an unresolvable pin or a bad credential will recover unattended.
REPLACEMENT:
The record also states the recovery expectation: whether an automatic retry is scheduled or the configuration or credentials must be corrected, with the next attempt time present only when an automatic retry is scheduled. Repeating on the refresh interval is not evidence that an unresolvable pin or a bad credential will recover unattended.
